input.prompt: Image 1 is a simple top view plan, north up: the round stone fire circle at the right with a ring of low stone benches open on the side facing the path; a straight path of flat stones about seven meters long running west from the fire circle to a small brick dome temazcal (a Mexican sweat lodge) at the left, whose low wooden door faces the fire; all on one straight line, with a dark grove of trees around and behind the temazcal. The camera is at the black triangle, east of the fire, looking west. Image 2 shows the temazcal: a brick dome about the height of a person with a low wooden door. Image 3 shows the stone fire circle and the families at the fire. Make a real photograph at dusk from that camera spot: low, just behind the fire, looking straight west down the path. The fire burns in the foreground; a few people sit on the low stone benches on both sides of it, seen from the side and from behind, lit warm by the flames, with a clear gap in the seating straight ahead where the path starts. The straight stone path runs from that gap to the temazcal; its open door faces us and the fire and glows warm inside, and soft white steam rises off the dome. Behind it the dark grove, and the last warm dusk light low in the sky above the trees. Calm and quiet. In this view there are only the fire circle with its benches and people, the straight path, the temazcal, the trees and the sky. No other buildings, no barns, no sheds, no signs. Real photograph, Kodak Portra 400 look, natural true colors, soft fine grain, real camera optics. No text, no letters, no signs, no labels, no logos, no watermark anywhere.
